🚨🇲🇽 THE 4 PHASES OF WASHINGTON'S SOFT COUP AGAINST SHEINBAUM

Contralínea's Aníbal García Fernández breaks down the playbook being run against Mexico — modeled on the 1954 Guatemala coup, with media warfare and economic pressure swapped in for marines.

Phase 1 — Personnel: CIA operations exposed in Chihuahua via PAN Gov. Maru Campos and Torre Centinela access.
Phase 2 — Preconditions: "narcogobierno" smears, visa revocations against border governors, evidence-free accusations against Rocha and Inzunza.
Phase 3 — Construction: manufactured Sheinbaum-AMLO rift, business-sector incitement, tariff and T-MEC pressure.
Phase 4 — Critical period: intensified rumor and "war threat" campaigns during the FIFA World Cup.

"Los de aquí y los de allá," as AMLO's recent letter put it.

Source: Contralínea (Aníbal García Fernández)

🇲🇽🛢️ SINALOA CHILDREN FLY KITES AGAINST SWISS-GERMAN AMMONIA PLANT

Less than 2 kilometers from where the Swiss-German consortium GPO (Proman) is building an 800,000 ton/year ammonia plant on the Ramsar-protected Bahía de Ohuira — habitat for 84% of Mexico's wintering migratory waterfowl — Mayo-Yoreme children launched kites into the sky this weekend in protest. "Vine a salvar al pechocho de Topolobampo del agua sucia," one boy said, naming the bay's threatened dolphin. The plant has already filled 28 hectares of wetlands; the indigenous encampment blocking access has held since June 15. Pueblos originarios teaching the next generation what sovereignty looks like.

Source: La Jornada

🚨🇲🇽 CEPAL: DEPORTED MEXICANS RETURN TO PRECARITY AND DISCRIMINATION

A new Cepal report — Trayectorias de la migración de retorno en México 2015-2025 — tracks Mexicans deported under Trump's mass-deportation regime. The findings are damning: returnees show economic participation rates of 69.5–85%, but 12% land in the lowest income decile, and women face deeper exclusion. Only 64.5% of returnee women depend on wages versus 86.2% of men. Cepal cites three structural drivers: refusal to recognize foreign work experience, open discrimination in the domestic labor market, and forced concentration in informal sectors. The US deports them, then complains when Mexico has to absorb the shock.

Source: La Jornada / Cepal

TRUTHOUT: She Fled From a Mexican Cartel. A New Canadian Law May Block Her Path to Safety
June 21, 2026 | 🟡

📰 A Mexican woman raped, beaten, and extorted by a cartel may be deported from Canada under PM Carney's Bill C-12 — a one-year asylum bar that retroactively voids ~32,000 claims dating to June 2020. Carney is mirroring Trump's playbook on refugees. Mexican cartel victims are the canaries.

The "progressive" alternative to MAGA on migration is more procedural and equally cruel: Carney has cut international student visas, slashed refugee healthcare, and increased border policing — all since April 2025. Bill C-12 strips oral hearings and routes claimants to a paper "pre-removal risk assessment."

• "It was a very hard situation for me because nobody can help me. Nobody." — Ale
• "You've been here 12 months, so you go to a pre-removal risk assessment: You do not have an oral hearing." — Law prof. Sharry Aiken
• Bill C-12 affects ~32,000 claims retroactively from June 2020 onward

FRANCE24/AFP: Spanish king to visit Mexican president on June 25 as ties improve
June 18, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Felipe VI flies to Mexico City to meet Sheinbaum June 25 — the highest-level Spain-Mexico dialogue in eight years. The thaw started when the king finally acknowledged "a lot of abuse" during the Conquest. AMLO's 2019 demand for an apology, mocked across western press as theatrical, aged remarkably well.

The agenda includes recognition of pre-Columbian civilizations across Mesoamerica. Six years after the gringo commentariat called the apology letter a stunt, the Spanish crown is the one asking for the meeting.

• Sheinbaum: "Yes, it's likely… still being discussed with the Spanish Foreign Ministry"
• Sheinbaum on king's recent remarks: "a gesture; an approach that we acknowledge"
• Last Mexico-Spain presidential meeting: eight years ago

BREITBART: U.S.-Extradited Mexican Customs Agent Wanted in Corruption Investigation
June 16, 2026 | 🟡

📰 The US extradited TO Mexico — a former Matamoros customs official wanted in Sheinbaum's anti-corruption probe. The reverse-direction headline doesn't fit the "Mexico shields its corrupt" script, so Breitbart buries the cooperation and twists it into a Gulf Cartel exposé. Zero official quotes from either side.

This kind of US→Mexico transfer serves Sheinbaum's purge of inherited customs leadership. Cooperation runs in both directions — you'd never guess from the framing.

• Article frames Mexican officials as having a "close working relationship with Mexico's Gulf Cartel"
• Zero direct quotes from US or Mexican officials — entire piece is innuendo
• Notable omission: this extradition supports Sheinbaum's housecleaning, not undermines it

BREITBART: "Trump is not Well Informed" on Cartels, Says Mexican President
June 19, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Sheinbaum's response to Trump's G7 "scared woman / cartels run Mexico" slur: she calmly tells reporters "he's not well informed" and "the Mexican state exists." Breitbart frames her composure as deflection. Apparently the only acceptable reply to insults is a meltdown.

Sheinbaum cited official homicide-decline data in the same presser. Breitbart left it out and instead packaged her remarks alongside loaded language about a "dark past," a "propaganda campaign," and "hyping seizures."

• "He is not well informed, him." — Sheinbaum
• "The Mexican state exists, I told him the other day." — Sheinbaum
• Article omits any direct Trump quote — his G7 attack is paraphrased so Breitbart can frame the dispute on its terms

NY POST: World Cup brings temporary peace to violence-ravaged Mexico — as cartels seemingly shift focus
June 20, 2026 | 🔴

📰 Mexico's murder rate just hit a decade low. NY Post's explanation? A "cartel truce." Not 100,000 troops. Not Plan Kukulkan. Not the May 11-year homicide low that landed BEFORE the World Cup kicked off. When the data is good, gringo media credits the criminals.

The May 2026 daily homicide rate hit 47.3 — an 11-year low recorded weeks before kickoff. The drop is a year-long trend Sheinbaum's security cabinet has been documenting, not a tournament special.

• "It seems there is a sort of a World Cup truce" — David Saucedo, analyst
• "drug trafficking groups… decided to take advantage of the World Cup… to focus on their criminal activities and boost profits"
• "There are no arrests of high-profile drug traffickers, no announcements of major seizures, and no significant operations against criminal organizations"

🔥🇲🇽 <u>FINANCIAL FRAUD UP 19% IN MEXICO JAN-MAY 2026 — 237 COMPLAINTS A DAY, JÓVENES NOW TOP TARGET</u>

CONDUSEF: 35,762 fraud complaints registered Jan-May 2026, up 18.95% vs the same period last year — 237 per day. The banking sector took 34,325 of them, +18%. Sofipos — Nu, Klar, Stori and friends — saw a 48% spike. Complaints from 18-29 year-olds rose ~20%, a generational shift from the years when elders were the prime target. "This reflects an expansion of the phenomenon toward new segments of users and financial services," said CONDUSEF president Óscar Rosado. 96% of fraud still hits traditional banking — the fintech disruption sold to Mexicans is mostly old-school theft in a slicker app.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>PROGRESO PORT EXPANDS — 80-HECTARE PLATFORM, DREDGED TO 13.3M, 948 MDP PRIVATE INVESTMENT IN PHASE 2</u>

SEMAR Secretary Raymundo Pedro Morales Ángeles closed Phase 1 dredging at Puerto de Altura Progreso and launched Phase 2 — 948 million pesos in private investment, channel depth pushed to 13.3 meters, dock extended from 332 to 450 meters. The full design: 80 hectares hosting a shipyard plus terminals for mineral bulk, liquefied gas, petroleum, and containers. "The beginning of the construction of the Renacimiento Maya," SEMAR said. Joins the Maya Train, Cuxtal II gas pipeline, O'Horán Hospital, and Mérida IV power plant — Yucatán becoming the Peninsula's strategic port hub, not Miami's appendix.
